figures.alt: A two-part figure. On the left is a histogram showing the ideal and noisy measurement results. On the right is a reduced assignment matrix mapping probabilities from the noisy measured results to the ideal case.
A Bloch sphere with a shaded region near the zero-state pole. The region is a shrunken oblate spheroid.

A Bloch sphere with a shaded region extending to both poles along the vertical z axis, but shrunken in the x-y plane. The region is again a shrunken oblate spheroid, but this time still centered on the origin and shrunken toward the z-axis.
A Bloch sphere with a shaded region shrunken uniformly toward the center.

Small circuit diagrams showing that a gate error on a rotation could show up as misalignment (as in a slight erroneous rotation about Y when intending to rotate about X) or as over/under rotation (as in an erroneous extra rotation about X).

Four circuit diagrams showing how errors can propagate. If a qubit is not entangled with other qubits, an error is confined. Most qubits will be entangled with some others, and thus errors can propagate from one qubit to another.
A ten-qubit quantum circuit that has been transpiled and has many entangling and rotation layers.
The same ten-qubit quantum circuit as in the previous figure, but now similar layers have been "boxed", meaning they have been outlined in a red box.
An error susceptibility map is shown for errors of various types.
